question: I want my screenshot compared against our committed `home.png` but never replaced, so I set `"overwrite": "false"` and `"maxVariation": 0.02` on the step. Now every run reports SKIPPED: "Skipped: file already exists at `C:\docs\home.png`. Set `overwrite` to `true` to replace it." Why isn't it comparing, and what should I set?

facts.text: With `overwrite: "false"`, an existing file at `path` makes Doc Detective keep it and skip the capture, so the step is SKIPPED and no comparison runs; `maxVariation` has no effect.
To compare, use `overwrite: "aboveVariation"`, the default (or leave `overwrite` out); a difference within `maxVariation` passes and leaves the reference unchanged.
A difference above `maxVariation` returns WARNING rather than FAIL, and with `aboveVariation` it replaces the reference image with the new capture.

must_not: `overwrite: "false"` compares the new capture against the reference and only declines to replace it.
A difference above `maxVariation` fails the step.
`overwrite: "true"` compares against the reference and replaces it only when it drifts.

wrong.why: an overwrite value the schema lacks

wrong.answer: `"overwrite": "false"` is right: it compares the new capture against `home.png` and never replaces it. SKIPPED means the comparison found no difference beyond `maxVariation`, so there was nothing to report. A difference above `maxVariation` fails the step, so your CI still catches drift.

Remove `overwrite` from the step so it uses the default, and keep `maxVariation`.

```json
{ "screenshot": { "path": "home.png", "maxVariation": 0.02 } }
```
